name: forecast-answer-formats: multiple-choice cross-tool leg
description: A labeled corpus of realistic LLM multiple-choice answer formats, each with its intended per-option distribution, scored against two deployed forecasting-bot extractors (mv2-forecaster 0.1.7 and Metaculus forecasting-tools) to measure which valid formats each reads, silently drops, or misreads as a spurious forecast. Designed probe, not a frequency estimate from live logs.
made_with: AI, by MV2 of Munim, Inc.

mv2_forecaster.rule: per option, line-anchored; tolerates leading whitespace, emphasis (* _ ~ `), '>' quote, '-', bullet, and an optional numbered marker; REQUIRES a literal ':' separator; '%' optional; all options must match or the whole run is dropped.
mv2_forecaster.status: source-grounded transcription; MC behaviour also confirmed by real sandbox runs (compete: forecaster-mc-fix-v1, forecaster-parser-audit-v1)

forecasting_tools.rule: per option, line-anchored on each stripped+lowercased line; tolerates leading non-word chars (emphasis/bullets); delimiter is ':' OR table-pipe '|'; no non-space chars allowed between the delimiter and the number; cannot cross a leading digit (numbered lists); exactly one matching line per option required or the run is dropped; infers decimal vs percentage then renormalises.
forecasting_tools.status: source-grounded transcription; pending independent live-package confirmation (compete: mc-xtool-verify)

classes.correct: returns all options within tolerance of the intended distribution
classes.miss: returns nothing for an answer that was actually present (silent drop)
classes.wrong_value: returns a distribution that differs from the intended one
classes.false_positive: returns a distribution when no forecast was intended
classes.correct_reject: returns nothing when no forecast was intended

multiple_choice.note: CONTRAST: mv2 pads the emphasis around the colon and reads it; forecasting-tools allows no non-space chars between the delimiter and the number, so '**' after the colon drops the whole run.
CONTRAST: mv2 has an explicit numbered-list prefix; forecasting-tools' leading \W* cannot cross the digit '1', so no option matches and the run is dropped.
CONTRAST (opposite direction): forecasting-tools accepts the table-pipe delimiter; mv2 requires a literal ':' so it drops the run.
Shared drop: neither accepts '=' as a separator.
Shared drop: no ':' or '|' delimiter before the number.

multiple_choice.text:
For reference, here are last year's frequencies, which are NOT my forecast:
Option A | 12
Option B | 88
I don't have enough information to forecast this question.
multiple_choice.note: FP TRAP: forecasting-tools' pipe support reads the reference frequency table as a forecast (12/88); mv2 requires a ':' so it correctly returns nothing. Mirror of the binary base-rate false positive, but driven by table syntax rather than last-%-wins.
